problems.title: Constants that differ

parts.prompt: Lanes in an AMD CDNA wavefront?
Bits in a ballot mask there?

problems.solution: 64 lanes, 64-bit masks. & 31 silently breaks on 64-wide hardware.

problems.title: The bug that compiles
problems.statement: A warp reduction loops for (o = 16; o > 0; o /= 2) v += shfl_down(v, o) and lane 0 writes the result. Run on 64-wide wavefronts.

options: Lane 0 holds the sum of only lanes 0–31; half the data is missing

hints: The first offset must cover half the width.
problems.solution: Offsets 16..1 reduce 32 lanes; lanes 32–63 never combine into lane 0. Starting at warpSize/2 fixes it. This exact bug is common in hipified code.

problems.title: Warps per block

parts.prompt: Shared array sized blockDim.x / 32 for per-warp partials on CDNA is…
options: fine for correctness, but loops that assume 8 partials read garbage

problems.solution: 8 and 4. Sizing by 32 over-allocates harmlessly, but code that then reads 8 partials when only 4 were written reads uninitialised memory.

problems.title: Occupancy on a different GPU
problems.statement: A kernel uses 128 registers per thread. An NVIDIA SM has 65,536 registers. In a simplified model of an AMD CDNA compute unit, each of its 4 SIMD units holds up to 4 wavefronts when each lane uses 128 vector registers.
problems.solution: 16 warps of 32 (512 threads) versus 16 wavefronts of 64 (1,024 threads): same register count, different occupancy in threads. Tuning parameters don't transfer; re-tune per target.

problems.title: Portable building blocks
problems.statement: The most portable way to write a block reduction is…

options: a library primitive (CUB / hipCUB / your own parameterised by warpSize)

hints: Let someone else handle the width.
problems.solution: Library primitives, or your Part 3 code parameterised by warpSize. Hand-rolled warp tricks are where the constants hide.

problems.title: Matrix units

options: nothing: rewrite with MFMA intrinsics or a library (rocWMMA, Composable Kernel)
the same WMMA API natively on every GPU

problems.solution: Matrix instructions and their fragment layouts are vendor-specific. rocWMMA offers a WMMA-like API on AMD; portable high-level code uses libraries or compilers (Triton, which targets both).

problems.title: Memory model differences

parts.prompt: Is it safe on Volta+ NVIDIA GPUs?
options: No: independent thread scheduling may interleave lanes
It may happen to work, which is worse: it hides the bug until it runs elsewhere

problems.solution: Unsafe on NVIDIA since Volta; may work on AMD today. Use explicit synchronisation everywhere.

problems.title: Compilers across targets
problems.statement: Triton compiles the same kernel for NVIDIA and AMD.

parts.prompt: What must change per target, in the compiler?

problems.solution: Layouts, widths and resource limits are the compiler's job per backend; that's exactly what a GPU compiler engineer builds.

problems.title: Testing portability
problems.statement: You port a CUDA kernel with hipify.

options: Run the full correctness suite, including warp-size-sensitive sizes (e.g. 33, 65, 1000 elements)

problems.solution: Compilation is the easy part. Tests at sizes that cross warp and wavefront boundaries catch the hidden 32s.

problems.title: SYCL sub-groups
problems.statement: Intel GPUs let the kernel choose a sub-group size of 8, 16 or 32.

parts.prompt: A reduction written for fixed 32 on a sub-group of 16…
options: reads lanes that don't exist or misses data

problems.solution: Width must be a parameter of the algorithm, read from the platform, not assumed.
